title: Height-one integration and the differential Hom correspondence
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of prime characteristic $p>0$ [def-weil-field]. Let $\mathfrak l$ be a finite-dimensional $k$-Lie algebra [def-wf-lie-algebra, def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] with a restricted operation $x\mapsto x^{[p]}$ satisfying the identities of [def-sfb-restricted-enveloping-algebra], and let $u(\mathfrak l)=T_k(\mathfrak l)/(xy-yx-[x,y],x^p-x^{[p]})$ be the algebra defined there. Give it the Hopf structure with $\Delta(x)=x\otimes1+1\otimes x$, $\varepsilon(x)=0$, $S(x)=-x$. The algebra $u(\mathfrak l)$ is finite-dimensional. Its linear dual, with Hopf operations dual to these, is a commutative Hopf algebra, and $\mathcal G(\mathfrak l)=\operatorname{Spec}(u(\mathfrak l)^\vee)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is a finite affine $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]. Its coordinate algebra is local, its augmentation ideal $I$ satisfies $a^p=0$ for every $a\in I$, and there is a natural restricted Lie isomorphism $\eta_{\mathfrak l}:\mathfrak l\simeq\operatorname{Lie}(\mathcal G(\mathfrak l))$. For an affine finite-type $k$-group $K$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $\operatorname{Lie}(K)$ means the tangent space at the identity [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space], with bracket from invariant derivations and restricted operation their $p$th composition. For every commutative $k$-algebra $A$, extension of scalars [def-pc-base-change] and differentiation give a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{A\text{-groups}}(\mathcal G(\mathfrak l)_A,K_A)\;\simeq\;\operatorname{Hom}_{A\text{-restricted Lie}}(A\otimes_k\mathfrak l,\operatorname{Lie}(K_A/A)).$$
On the right, maps are $A$-linear and preserve bracket and the $p$th operation defined by relative invariant derivations. This bijection sends $f$ to $df\circ(\eta_{\mathfrak l})_A$ and is natural in $A$, $K$ and $\mathfrak l$. Integration and $\eta$ commute with every field extension of $k$. When $A=k$ and the restricted Lie map is injective, its integrated group homomorphism is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Propositions 11.35--11.37 and the first sentence of the proof of Corollary 11.38, printed pp.222--223; Definition 10.39 and Theorem 10.40, pp.206--207. The relative Hom formula is the finite-dual Hopf-algebra formulation of Proposition 11.36, valid after a commutative base-algebra extension, not an appeal to geometric-point faithfulness. The correction to Proposition 11.36 in the book errata, Chapter 11 errata entry for p.223, removes the duplicated Lie(phi).

proof.text: Write $B=u(\mathfrak l)$ and choose an ordered basis $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ of $\mathfrak l$. Restricted PBW gives the basis $e^a=e_1^{a_1}\cdots e_n^{a_n}$, $0\le a_i<p$, of $B$, including $1=e^0$. In particular $\dim B=p^n$ and $\mathfrak l\to B$ is injective. Define $\Delta,\varepsilon,S$ on tensor generators as in the statement. They descend to the quotient: bracket relations go to zero because the two tensor factors commute; the commuting binomial formula in characteristic $p$ gives $(x\otimes1+1\otimes x)^p=x^p\otimes1+1\otimes x^p$, so restricted relations also go to zero. The counit kills both types of relation; reversal with $S(x)=-x$ sends bracket relations to their negatives and restricted relations to $(-1)^p(x^p-x^{[p]})$.

Coassociativity, the counit equations and cocommutativity hold on $1$ and each $x\in\mathfrak l$, hence on all products, since the maps in these equations are algebra maps. For the antipode, if $\sum S(a_1)a_2=\varepsilon(a)$ and $\sum S(b_1)b_2=\varepsilon(b)$, then $\sum S(a_1b_1)a_2b_2=\sum S(b_1)S(a_1)a_2b_2=\varepsilon(a)\varepsilon(b)$; the opposite antipode identity has the reversed calculation. Induction on words proves both identities. Thus $B$ is a cocommutative Hopf algebra generated by primitive elements. The finite-dual lemma makes $H=B^\vee$ a commutative Hopf algebra. Its spectrum is a group by the Hopf-spectrum construction and is finite since its coordinate algebra has the finite dual PBW basis.

source.place: Section 11h, p.222, Hopf identities; Proposition 11.35, pp.222--223; Proposition 3.6, p.66

proof.text: Let $z_a\in H$ be dual to $e^a$ and put $y_i=z_{\delta_i}$. Expanding the coproduct of the ordered PBW monomial gives $\Delta(e^a)=\sum_{b\le a}(\prod_i\binom{a_i}{b_i})e^b\otimes e^{a-b}$. Hence $z_bz_c=(\prod_i\binom{b_i+c_i}{b_i})z_{b+c}$ when every $b_i+c_i<p$, and zero otherwise. Therefore $\prod_i y_i^{a_i}=(\prod_i a_i!)z_a$ and $y_i^p=0$. All $a_i!$ with $a_i<p$ are units in $k$. These formulas give an augmented algebra isomorphism $H\simeq k[y_1,\ldots,y_n]/(y_1^p,\ldots,y_n^p)$, by matching the displayed basis monomials. Thus $I=(y_1,\ldots,y_n)$, $I^{n(p-1)+1}=0$ and $H/I=k$. Every element outside $I$ is a nonzero scalar times $1$ plus a nilpotent, so is invertible by a finite geometric series. Thus $H$ is local. The characteristic-$p$ binomial formula gives $a^p=0$ for every $a\in I$.

source.place: Proposition 11.35, pp.222--223, height-one assertion supplied explicitly from Theorem 10.40

proof.text: A tangent vector of $\operatorname{Spec}H$ at its augmentation is exactly an algebra map $H\to k[\epsilon]/\epsilon^2$ reducing to the augmentation, hence is $h\mapsto h(1)+\epsilon v(h)$ with $v$ an augmentation derivation. The relative tangent-calculus lemma identifies this space with $(I/I^2)^\vee$. The classes of the $y_i$ form its dual basis by step 3. Evaluation on $e_i\in B$ sends $y_j$ to $\delta_{ij}$ and is an augmentation derivation because $e_i$ is primitive. Thus $\eta(x)(h)=h(x)$ is a linear isomorphism. Under finite-dual evaluation, convolution of functionals on $H$ is multiplication in $B$. The relative tangent-calculus lemma therefore identifies bracket and $[p]$ on these tangent vectors with $xy-yx$ and $x^p$. The defining relations in $B$ prove that $\eta$ preserves both operations.

source.place: Propositions 10.28--10.29, pp.195--196; Propositions 11.35--11.37, pp.222--223, canonical tangent identification

proof.text: Now let $A$ be any commutative $k$-algebra and put $C=A\otimes_k k[K]$ and $B_A=A\otimes_k B$. The coordinate Hopf structure of $K$ extends by the same formulas to $C$; finite-dual base change identifies $H_A=A\otimes_k H$ with $B_A^\vee$. The same $y_i$ presentation over $A$ identifies the relative tangent space of $\operatorname{Spec}H_A$ with $A\otimes_k\mathfrak l$ by evaluation, with its bracket and restricted operation from $B_A$. For a restricted $A$-Lie map $\alpha:A\otimes_k\mathfrak l\to L_C$, send $x\in\mathfrak l$ to the functional $\alpha(1\otimes x)\in\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,A)$ with convolution multiplication. Relative tangent calculus says its commutator and $p$th convolution power equal the prescribed Lie operations. Thus all bracket and restricted relations vanish. The tensor-quotient presentation, followed by scalar extension, gives the unique algebra map $r_\alpha:B_A\to\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,A)$ with these generator values. Each is an augmentation derivation, so the finite-dual primitive-generator criterion makes $t_\alpha(c)(b)=r_\alpha(b)(c)$ a Hopf map $C\to H_A$. Taking spectra gives the integrated group homomorphism $\mathcal G(\mathfrak l)_A\to K_A$.

source.place: Proposition 11.36, p.223, finite-dual version of integration over A; Definition 10.39 and its universal property, pp.206--207

proof.text: Conversely, a group homomorphism gives its coordinate Hopf map $t:C\to H_A$ by affine-spectrum duality and compatibility with multiplication, identity and inverse. Its transpose $r(b)(c)=t(c)(b)$ is a convolution algebra map by the finite-dual criterion. Its values on $1\otimes\mathfrak l$ are augmentation derivations; since $r$ preserves the relations $xy-yx=[x,y]$ and $x^p=x^{[p]}$, these values define a restricted $A$-Lie map. This is $df\circ\eta_A$: evaluating a tangent vector on $c$ gives exactly $t(c)(1\otimes x)$. The two constructions are inverse because both transpose twice to the same pairing and an algebra map from $B_A$ is determined by these generators. This proves bijectivity with the asserted differential description. It also proves naturality: precomposition in $\mathfrak l$ restricts the generators, a homomorphism $K\to K'$ precomposes coordinate functions, and a map $A\to A'$ extends the pairings; in each case both constructions have the same values $r(x)(c)$.

source.place: Proposition 11.36, p.223, uniqueness and naturality; errata for p.223, printed p.644, correcting its differential formula

proof.text: For a field extension $F/k$, the two presentations of $u(F\otimes_k\mathfrak l)$ and $F\otimes_k B$ are identified by $1\otimes x\mapsto1\otimes x$: the relations for basis generators agree, and restricted PBW says these generate all relations and give the same ordered basis. Their coproducts, counits and antipodes agree on generators. Finite-dual base change identifies their coordinate Hopf algebras. Evaluation defining $\eta$ has the same values on tensors on both sides. Consequently integration and $\eta$ commute with every field extension, including inseparable extensions.

source.place: Theorems 10.39--10.40, pp.206--207, and Proposition 11.35, pp.222--223: scalar extension of the presentations and finite-dual evaluation

proof.text: Finally take $A=k$ and suppose $\alpha$ is injective. Write $J=\ker(k[K]\to k)$. Finite generation of $k[K]$ implies that $J/J^2$ is finite-dimensional: if $c_j$ generate the algebra, the elements $c_j-\varepsilon(c_j)$ generate $J$. The dual of the induced cotangent map $J/J^2\to I/I^2$ is $\alpha$ by the differential formula. The finite-dimensional dual-rank equality therefore makes that cotangent map surjective. Choose $c_i\in J$ whose images $b_i\in I$ under the coordinate map have classes forming a basis of $I/I^2$. Since $I$ is nilpotent, these $b_i$ generate $H$ as a $k$-algebra: products of $r$ of them span $I^r/I^{r+1}$ by expanding products after $I=(\sum_i kb_i)+I^2$; subtract such products successively for $r=1,\ldots,n(p-1)$, and the remainder is zero. Thus the coordinate map is surjective. The affine characterization of a closed immersion gives the desired conclusion. When $n=0$, $H=k$ and this is just its augmentation, still surjective.

source.place: First sentence of Corollary 11.38 proof, p.223: embedding from an injective restricted Lie map; explicit nilpotent-cotangent argument

proof_origin.place: Propositions 11.35--11.37 and Corollary 11.38, pp.222--223; PBW coordinate computation, relative finite-dual argument and embedding proof filled in explicitly where Milne refers elsewhere
